processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steels produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots.
Hot-rolled products followed by water quenching (as-received condition).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers macro-hardness, 5 kg load, 5 indentations per sample, hot-rolled (as-received) condition

unmapped_findings: The 12Al-10Mn-1C alloy recorded the highest hot-rolled (as-received) hardness among the tested Fe–Mn–Al–C grades at 401 HV (Table 5, also Table 4 and Table 9).

Hot-rolled 12Al-10Mn-1C serves as the as-received reference condition for the study; no austenite transformation is described for the hot-rolled state itself, only for the 600 °C and 800 °C tempered conditions.

Comparative (involves other samples): 800 °C tempering left the hardness of 12Al-10Mn-1C essentially unchanged (hot-rolled 401 HV vs 800 °C tempered 399 HV), attributed to its wide inter-lamellar spacing (Table 5, Table 9).

No phase-volume-fraction (CALPHAD) diagram is provided for the 12Al-10Mn-1C composition; the diagrams in the paper cover 9Al-10Mn-0.4C, 9Al-10Mn-1C, 9Al-20Mn-1C, 9Al-30Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C.
